text:
sarah: @here noticing sustained network latency in eu-west1 since ~08:12 UTC. Multiple inference pods reporting 502/524, autoscaler not bringing up new GPU nodes fast enough. GPU pool util down to 40% but pending pods stuck in Pending state.

mike: which path is failing? east-west peering or GCP egress?

sarah: appears internal GCE interconnect to our CDN edges is dropping packets intermittently. gcp console shows packet loss on peering.

gcp-status-bot: [08:15 UTC] Incident: Interconnect - Europe region experiencing intermittent packet loss affecting peering and egress. More info: https://status.gcp.example/incident/12345

lee: seeing a surge of 524s from Fastly edges to our origin. CDN is retrying and causing bursts to our frontends, which backpressure to edge-proxies and into inference hosts.

ara: @sarah can you post the pod events?

sarah: sure, tailing one host events:

```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age                From               Message
  ----     ------             ----               ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled          5m                 default-scheduler  Successfully assigned infra/inf-abc to node-gpu-3
  Warning  FailedScheduling   4m (x12 over 5m)   kube-scheduler     0/5 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu, 2 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
  Normal   Pulling            3m                 kubelet            Pulling image "redwood/inference:stable"
  Warning  BackOff            2m                 kubelet            Back-off pulling image "redwood/inference:stable"
```

mike: interesting — scheduler thinks GPUs insufficient even though util down. Could be node-controller marking nodes NotReady?

lee: checking node status: some nodes show network probe failed and CNI flaps.

ara: workaround thoughts: 1) divert traffic from eu-west1 to eu-west3/us-west temporarily 2) increase dedicated burst capacity from reserved pools in us-west 3) enable degraded crypto path (rotate to local ephemeral keys) if KMS is impacted 4) lower concurrency settings on frontends to reduce retries.

sarah: starting traffic shift and lowering concurrency now. Running playbook step:

```
# shift routes away from eu-west1
rbctl routes set --region eu-west1 --weight 0 --to-regions eu-west3,us-west1 --reason "gcp interconnect packet loss"
# reduce frontend concurrency
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/frontend MAX_CONCURRENCY=2
```

deploy-bot: @sarah triggered rollout: routes updated (change-id: r-3321) and frontend env updated (deploy/frontend v1.42 -> v1.43).

mike: can we also spin up temporary on-demand GPUs in eu-west1 via cloud provider to ease scheduling pressure? Costly but faster than cross-region latency.

lee: I can request 10 on-demand V100s in eu-west1. Provisioning request submitted. ETA ~7 minutes.

gcp-status-bot: [08:23 UTC] Update: Interconnect packet loss persists; GCP engineers investigating.

ara: while that spins up, enable model fallback to smaller-quantized variant for latency-sensitive routes. Lower token cap to reduce per-request duration.

sarah: toggled fallback rules in routing config. JSON snippet:

```
{
  "route":"/v1/generate",
  "fallback_models":["redwood-small-quant","redwood-xq-lite"],
  "max_tokens":256
}
```

lee: nodes are coming up but kubelet still logs CNI error on dhcp renewal. I think the interconnect packet loss causes metadata server timeouts and that breaks node bootstrap.

mike: can we use hostNetwork on node-level agents to bypass CNI for bootstrap? Risky but may allow kubelet to finish registration.

lee: applied hostNetwork to bootstrap DaemonSet. Re-deploying.

sarah: traffic shifted, initial 30% of requests now routed out of eu-west1. Error rate dropped from 6% -> 1.7% in last 3 mins.

ara: good. keep an eye on tail latency and error budgets. Also coordinate with support to get KMS status — if interconnect affects KMS calls we should prepare a key-rotation/ephemeral plan.

mike: support contacted GCP and Fastly for upstream mitigation. Requesting BGP-level reroute on GCP side.

gcp-status-bot: [08:37 UTC] Update: GCP confirmed partial packet loss due to link asymmetry; mitigation steps in progress.

lee: on-demand GPUs are registered and ready. Autoscaler still conservative, bumping desired replica count now.

sarah: increasing autoscaler thresholds and forcing scale:

```
kubectl scale --replicas=18 deploy/inference-gpu -n infra
```

deploy-bot: Scale request accepted; new pods scheduled (IDs: inf-901..inf-918).

ara: if packet loss persists longer than 30m we should consider proactive region failover for customer-critical tenants. Prepare runbook and notify CSM.

sarah: agreed. I'll open an incident page and ping CSMs. Creating incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/IR-2026-024-eu-net

mike: postmortem notes to collect: scheduler misinterpreting capacity (Insufficient gpu while underutilized), CNI resilience on metadata timeouts, autoscaler conservative defaults, CDN retry amplification.

lee: putting a short-term mitigation list in the incident doc: hostNetwork bootstrap, route shift, on-demand GPUs, fallback models, reduce frontend concurrency.

ara: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread. once GCP confirms full mitigation we'll start rolling traffic back gradually. :white_check_mark:
